title: Certified Defense on the Fairness of Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Malicious attackers can corrupt the fairness of GNN predictions by perturbing input graph data.

gap.claim: Certifiable defense for the fairness of GNNs is presented as a problem requiring study.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes ELEGANT, a principled framework for certifiable defense of GNN fairness.
The paper provides a theoretical certification analysis for GNN fairness.
ELEGANT is designed as a plug-and-play framework that can use any GNN backbone without assumptions about its structure or parameters or requiring retraining.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize certifiable defense on the fairness level of GNNs as a novel problem.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on real-world datasets.
The authors report effectiveness across different GNN backbones and parameter settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are prominent models for graph-based tasks.
Input-graph perturbations can corrupt the fairness of GNN predictions.
The paper studies certifiable defense for GNN fairness.
ELEGANT provides a principled framework and theoretical certification analysis, with applicability to arbitrary GNN backbones under stated perturbation budgets without retraining.
The authors report experiments on real-world datasets across GNN backbones and parameter settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not define the fairness metric or certification guarantee.
The abstract does not specify the perturbation budgets or theoretical conditions.
The abstract does not identify the datasets, baselines, or quantitative experimental results.
The abstract does not describe ELEGANT's implementation details.
